title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 370
paragraphs: and I have made mention of the oracle in Egypt often before this, and I will now give an account of it, since it is worth describing. This oracle in Egypt is sacred to Leto and is established in a great city near the mouth of the Nile called the Sebennytic, as one sails up the river from the sea; and the name of this city where the oracle is found is Buto, as I have said before. In this Buto there is a temple of Apollo and Artemis; and the temple-house of Leto, in which the oracle is, is both great in itself and has a gateway ten fathoms in height. But what most astonished me of the things to be seen there, I will now describe. Within this sacred enclosure stands a shrine of Leto made of a single stone, both in height and in length, of which all the walls in these two directions are equal, each being forty cubits; and for the covering of the roof another stone lies on top, with a cornice measuring four cubits.
